q: What is the scientific name of the African Grey Parrot?
a: Psittacus erithacus

q: What is the IUCN status of Psittacus erithacus?
a: EN (EN)

q: Where does the African Grey Parrot live?
a: West & Central Africa rainforest belt, Ghana, Cameroon, DR Congo, Ivory Coast

q: What does the African Grey Parrot eat?
a: Seeds, nuts, fruits, berries, palm nuts; occasional bark and blossoms

q: Describe the African Grey Parrot.
a: African Grey Parrot (Psittacus erithacus) is a Psittacidae of order Psittaciformes. Dense lowland rainforest, gallery forest, savanna-edge mangroves. Loud screech 'kraa-kraa'; exceptional mimicry of human speech and environmental sounds

q: What is the scientific name of the Greater Flamingo?
a: Phoenicopterus roseus

q: What is the IUCN status of Phoenicopterus roseus?
a: LC (LC)

q: Where does the Greater Flamingo live?
a: East Africa (Rift Valley lakes), North Africa, Saharan salt lakes, Southern Africa (Etosha, Makgadikgadi)

q: What does the Greater Flamingo eat?
a: Blue-green algae, diatoms, brine shrimp, molluscs strained through lamellae

q: Describe the Greater Flamingo.
a: Greater Flamingo (Phoenicopterus roseus) is a Phoenicopteridae of order Phoenicopteriformes. Alkaline and hypersaline lakes, lagoons, estuaries; feeds in shallow water. Goose-like honking 'ka-ha-ha'; nasal 'ung-ung-ung' contact calls

q: What is the scientific name of the Yellow-billed Stork?
a: Mycteria ibis

q: What is the IUCN status of Mycteria ibis?
a: LC (LC)

q: Where does the Yellow-billed Stork live?
a: Sub-Saharan Africa, East Africa, Southern Africa, Senegal to Ethiopia

q: What does the Yellow-billed Stork eat?
a: Fish, frogs, insects, crustaceans; tactile-foraging in murky water

q: Describe the Yellow-billed Stork.
a: Yellow-billed Stork (Mycteria ibis) is a Ciconiidae of order Ciconiiformes. Freshwater marshes, floodplains, rice paddies, lake margins. Mostly silent; bill-clattering at nest

q: What is the scientific name of the Common Ostrich?
a: Struthio camelus

q: What is the IUCN status of Struthio camelus?
a: LC (LC)

q: Where does the Common Ostrich live?
a: Sahel to Southern Africa, East African savanna, Kalahari, Serengeti

q: What does the Common Ostrich eat?
a: Omnivorous: seeds, grasses, shrubs, insects, small vertebrates

q: Describe the Common Ostrich.
a: Common Ostrich (Struthio camelus) is a Struthionidae of order Struthioniformes. Open savanna, semi-desert, dry grasslands. Low booming 'booh-boooh' from males; hissing when threatened

q: What is the scientific name of the Secretary Bird?
a: Sagittarius serpentarius

q: What is the IUCN status of Sagittarius serpentarius?
a: VU (VU)

q: Where does the Secretary Bird live?
a: Sub-Saharan Africa, East Africa, Southern Africa savanna

q: What does the Secretary Bird eat?
a: Snakes (incl. venomous), lizards, rodents, large insects, small birds

q: Describe the Secretary Bird.
a: Secretary Bird (Sagittarius serpentarius) is a Sagittariidae of order Accipitriformes. Open grassland, savanna, semi-arid steppe. Croaking 'kurr-kurr'; usually silent away from nest

q: What is the scientific name of the Lilac-breasted Roller?
a: Coracias caudatus

q: What is the IUCN status of Coracias caudatus?
a: LC (LC)

q: Where does the Lilac-breasted Roller live?
a: Eastern & Southern Africa, Kenya, Tanzania, Botswana, Zimbabwe

q: What does the Lilac-breasted Roller eat?
a: Insects, grasshoppers, beetles, small reptiles; hawks from perches

q: Describe the Lilac-breasted Roller.
a: Lilac-breasted Roller (Coracias caudatus) is a Coraciidae of order Coraciiformes. Open woodland, savanna with scattered trees, cultivated land. Rolling, grating 'rak-rak-rak' and harsh 'aaak'

q: What is the scientific name of the African Fish Eagle?
a: Haliaeetus vocifer

q: What is the IUCN status of Haliaeetus vocifer?
a: LC (LC)

q: Where does the African Fish Eagle live?
a: Sub-Saharan Africa near water, Lake Victoria, Okavango Delta, Zambezi

q: What does the African Fish Eagle eat?
a: Fish (snatched from surface), waterbirds, carrion

q: Describe the African Fish Eagle.
a: African Fish Eagle (Haliaeetus vocifer) is a Accipitridae of order Accipitriformes. Lakes, rivers, reservoirs, coastline with abundant fish. Iconic yelping 'weee-ah-koh-koh-koh' — the 'voice of Africa'

q: What is the scientific name of the Grey Crowned Crane?
a: Balearica regulorum

q: What is the IUCN status of Balearica regulorum?
a: EN (EN)

q: Where does the Grey Crowned Crane live?
a: East Africa, Southern Africa, Uganda, Kenya, South Africa

q: What does the Grey Crowned Crane eat?
a: Grass tips, seeds, insects, frogs, small fish

q: Describe the Grey Crowned Crane.
a: Grey Crowned Crane (Balearica regulorum) is a Gruidae of order Gruiformes. Wetlands, upland grasslands, croplands near water. Resonant honking 'ou-ou-ou' with a dancing display

q: What is the scientific name of the Southern Ground Hornbill?
a: Bucorvus leadbeateri

q: What is the IUCN status of Bucorvus leadbeateri?
a: VU (VU)

q: Where does the Southern Ground Hornbill live?
a: Southern Africa, Botswana, Zimbabwe, NE South Africa, southern Kenya

q: What does the Southern Ground Hornbill eat?
a: Insects, reptiles, small mammals, birds, frogs

q: Describe the Southern Ground Hornbill.
a: Southern Ground Hornbill (Bucorvus leadbeateri) is a Bucorvidae of order Bucerotiformes. Savanna, open woodland, grassland with large trees for nesting. Deep booming 'oom-oom-oom' audible over 3 km

q: What is the scientific name of the Shoebill?
a: Balaeniceps rex

q: What is the IUCN status of Balaeniceps rex?
a: VU (VU)

q: Where does the Shoebill live?
a: Central & East Africa swamps, Sudan, Uganda, Zambia, DR Congo

q: What does the Shoebill eat?
a: Lungfish, catfish, snakes, baby crocodiles; strike-and-gulp

q: Describe the Shoebill.
a: Shoebill (Balaeniceps rex) is a Balaenicipitidae of order Pelecaniformes. Papyrus and reed swamps, poorly oxygenated marshes. Bill-clattering like a machine gun; rarely vocal otherwise

q: What is the scientific name of the Kori Bustard?
a: Ardeotis kori

q: What is the IUCN status of Ardeotis kori?
a: NT (NT)

q: Where does the Kori Bustard live?
a: Southern & East Africa, Kalahari, Serengeti, Etosha

q: What does the Kori Bustard eat?
a: Insects, lizards, small mammals, seeds, berries

q: Describe the Kori Bustard.
a: Kori Bustard (Ardeotis kori) is a Otididae of order Otidiformes. Semi-arid savanna, grassland, open woodland. Deep booming 'oomf' from inflated throat; usually quiet

q: What is the scientific name of the Helmeted Guineafowl?
a: Numida meleagris

q: What is the IUCN status of Numida meleagris?
a: LC (LC)

q: Where does the Helmeted Guineafowl live?
a: Sub-Saharan Africa, Widespread, Also feral in the Americas/Europe

q: What does the Helmeted Guineafowl eat?
a: Seeds, roots, insects, ticks, small invertebrates

q: Describe the Helmeted Guineafowl.
a: Helmeted Guineafowl (Numida meleagris) is a Numididae of order Galliformes. Savanna, open woodland, farmland, scrub. Loud 'kek-kek-kek-kek-kek' alarm chatter

q: What is the scientific name of the Tawny Eagle?
a: Aquila rapax

q: What is the IUCN status of Aquila rapax?
a: VU (VU)

q: Where does the Tawny Eagle live?
a: Sahel to Southern Africa, East Africa, India (subspecies)

q: What does the Tawny Eagle eat?
a: Carrion, small mammals, birds, reptiles, insects

q: Describe the Tawny Eagle.
a: Tawny Eagle (Aquila rapax) is a Accipitridae of order Accipitriformes. Arid savanna, desert edge, open grassland. Weak, high-pitched 'kee-kee' and barking notes

q: What is the scientific name of the Yellow-billed Oxpecker?
a: Buphagus africanus

q: What is the IUCN status of Buphagus africanus?
a: LC (LC)

q: Where does the Yellow-billed Oxpecker live?
a: Sub-Saharan Africa (west of Rift), Savanna with large mammals

q: What does the Yellow-billed Oxpecker eat?
a: Ticks and ectoparasites from large mammals; blood and wound tissue

q: Describe the Yellow-billed Oxpecker.
a: Yellow-billed Oxpecker (Buphagus africanus) is a Buphagidae of order Passeriformes. Open woodland and savanna with herds of ungulates. Hissing 'sss-sss' and shrill chirps

q: What is the scientific name of the African Penguin?
a: Spheniscus demersus

q: What is the IUCN status of Spheniscus demersus?
a: CR (CR)

q: Where does the African Penguin live?
a: Southern African coastline, South Africa, Namibia, Benguela upwelling

q: What does the African Penguin eat?
a: Anchovies, sardines, squid, small crustaceans

q: Describe the African Penguin.
a: African Penguin (Spheniscus demersus) is a Spheniscidae of order Sphenisciformes. Rocky offshore islands and mainland burrows near cold currents. Braying 'bray-bray' like a donkey; hence 'jackass penguin'

q: What is the scientific name of the Crowned Lapwing?
a: Vanellus coronatus

q: What is the IUCN status of Vanellus coronatus?
a: LC (LC)

q: Where does the Crowned Lapwing live?
a: Sub-Saharan Africa, East & Southern Africa dry grasslands

q: What does the Crowned Lapwing eat?
a: Insects, termites, beetles, seeds

a: Crowned Lapwing (Vanellus coronatus) is a Charadriidae of order Charadriiformes. Short grassland, fallow fields, dry savanna. Sharp 'kik-kik-kik' alarm; whistled 'whee-whee'

q: What is the scientific name of the Violet-backed Starling?
a: Cinnyricinclus leucogaster

q: What is the IUCN status of Cinnyricinclus leucogaster?
a: LC (LC)

q: Where does the Violet-backed Starling live?
a: Sub-Saharan Africa, Woodland and forest edges

q: What does the Violet-backed Starling eat?

a: Violet-backed Starling (Cinnyricinclus leucogaster) is a Sturnidae of order Passeriformes. Open woodland, savanna with trees, gardens, forest edge. Whistled 'tsee-tsee' and soft warbling

q: What is the scientific name of the African Jacana?
a: Actophilornis africanus

q: What is the IUCN status of Actophilornis africanus?
a: LC (LC)

q: Where does the African Jacana live?
a: Sub-Saharan Africa, Freshwater wetlands with floating vegetation

q: What does the African Jacana eat?
a: Insects, seeds, molluscs picked from floating plants

q: What is the scientific name of the Hadada Ibis?

q: What is the IUCN status of Bostrychia hagedash?
a: LC (LC)

q: Where does the Hadada Ibis live?
a: Sub-Saharan Africa, Wetlands, lawns, urban parks
